g.text: Frequency + duty meter - the two numbers, and the twelve banked points
no packet: the PWM period IS the frame, and the payload is a 16-bit pair
WHY T IS RESET AT EVERY RISING EDGE IS THE WHOLE
The period could be computed as (now - last rising), but
that is a 16-BIT SUBTRACT and the ISA has no carry flag,
so the borrow of a-b cannot be read off the difference:
(a-b) mod 256 has two preimages, one positive and one
negative, for every value except zero. Getting it
exactly needs a four-case analysis on bit 7, and a
COMPARE is the same analysis again.
Resetting instead turns the question from "how long since
the last edge" into "how long since the edge that
started this one", which the counter answers by itself.
Two resets remove every subtract, every compare and
AND WHY H IS ALSO RESET AT THE RISING EDGE.
Same reason, different edge: H accumulates while the
line is high and simply STOPS when it goes low, so the
high time is whatever is in H at the next rising edge.
No subtraction, no comparison, and no divide - the duty
falls out of the pair rather than being computed.
THE TWELVE BANKED POINTS, as measured on real RTL
At 100 Hz the period is 10 000 us, which does not fit in
one 8-bit counter. A firmware that counts into a byte
for a 100 Hz signal: a wrong
ANSWER rather than a wrong precision, and a defect
no symptom at any other point in the sweep
So the counters are 16-bit, and the mutation gate
Three points are out by EXACTLY ONE TICK, and they are
printed as out rather than folded into a tolerance.
- and the duty follows to a tenth of a point (59.9,
39.9) because the two counts share the same edge
That is the resolution showing up in the log instead
of hiding in a tolerance, which is what a
measured-truth record should look like. A figure or a
page that printed "within 1 %" here would be hiding
the instrument's resolution in the one place a reader
The first six points are runs 0 and 1 (durations above
800 us); the last six are runs 2 to 5 (down to 80 us).
and ten different duties, so a firmware that is right at
one end and wrong at the other cannot pass by averaging.
a change to high RESETS both
a change to low STOPS H
the elapsed time is added in
